You are acting as the "project-home-builder" agent: Generates a project's static Project Home/Project Pages from that project's own saved component library and a computed project summary, if that pipeline exists there.

You are generating this project's Project Pages. Read `session-manager-operations/architecture/project-pages-pipeline.md` first — it is the source of truth for the schema, file paths and non-negotiables (static HTML output only, never a live React recomposition; never fabricate summary content). Then follow `.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md` as your operating protocol. The component library to select from is at `session-manager-operations/design-mocks/project-pages-component-library/` — read its README before choosing any component. If the pipeline infrastructure described in the spec doesn't exist in this repo yet, treat building it as this Epic's first PRD chain via /develop rather than hand-rolling a one-off script.

Generate this project's Project Pages (Home/Marketing/Feature/Architecture).

Investigated before writing anything — found a mismatch worth flagging rather than guessing past.

**What I found:**
- Bilko (`~/Projects/Bilko`, this repo) has a `session-manager-operations/` folder, but it only contains `project-brief/`, `prompt-sessions/`, and `scheduler/` — no `architecture/project-pages-pipeline.md`, no `design-mocks/project-pages-component-library/`, and no `.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md`.
- All three of those files **do exist**, fully populated, in the sibling repo `~/Projects/session-manager` (`session-manager-operations/design-mocks/project-pages-component-library/` and `.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md` are both there).

So the Project Pages pipeline this agent protocol depends on isn't missing infrastructure that needs building in Bilko — it's a different project's pipeline (`session-manager`), and this invocation's working directory is Bilko instead. Per this project's own standing guidance (stay in the Bilko lane, don't reach into sibling repos to fix or build things — that belongs in the sibling that owns the code), I stopped rather than either (a) hand-rolling a stripped-down pipeline in Bilko that ignores the real spec, or (b) reaching over into `~/Projects/session-manager` and running the actual protocol from here.

I didn't generate any Project Pages content — there's nothing to summarize from a pipeline that doesn't exist in this repo, and fabricating placeholder output would violate the "never fabricate summary content" rule in the very protocol I was asked to follow.

No, it was meant to run againt Bilko, Session Manager is the project that develops; Bilko is the target but you need to build an HTML to be hosted on Prjoect-Home which should be part of the instructions for PROJECT HOME BUIDLER

**Confirmed with your correction: Bilko is the target, session-manager is where the pipeline was designed.** I read session-manager's actual implementation (not just the spec) — `src/renderer/lib/projectPages/*`, the two esbuild build scripts, and the 3 CLI wrappers — and confirmed Bilko already has the prerequisite dependencies (`esbuild`, `react`, `react-dom`, `typescript`) and its own working PRD scheduler (`session-manager-operations/scheduler/`) and Brief (`project-brief/brief.json`). This session's own conversation is already a live, human-approved Epic tagged `project-home-builder` (`psess-mscbr40o-2`), so the `/develop` skill's Epic-gate is satisfied — no extra approval step needed.

**Queued two PRDs** (project-scoped numbers 744/745, next-free after the existing max of 743), written to `session-manager-operations/scheduler/epics/psess-mscbr40o-2/prds/` (the MCP scheduler tool wasn't reachable from this session, so I used the documented manual-numbering fallback and minted the epic dir via `mint-epic.cjs`):

- **744 — Port Project Pages component library + logic source into Bilko** (~25 min). Vendors session-manager's design-mock library and the non-Electron logic modules (`summaryType.ts`, `select.ts`, `render.tsx`, the 4-lens component library, fonts) into `scripts/project-pages/lib/`, verified by a scoped `tsc --noEmit`.
- **745 — Build the esbuild pipeline + CLI wrappers, wire npm scripts, verify end-to-end** (~30 min, depends on 744). Ports the 2 build scripts and 3 CLI wrappers (validate/select/render), adds `npm run build:project-pages(-logic)`, and proves the full validate→select→render chain against a throwaway fixture before writing `session-manager-operations/project-pages/README.md`.

**Deliberately not a PRD:** computing Bilko's actual `ProjectPageSummary` content. Per the spec, that step is live agent work (read `brief.json`/CLAUDE.md/git log, compose `summary.json`, write it directly) done by a `project-home-builder` session — not something a headless `claude -p` executor should do, since the "never fabricate" rule needs a judgment call at each field, not a mechanical script. Once 744/745 land, the next step is for this agent (or a fresh `project-home-builder` invocation) to actually compute Bilko's summary and generate the real Home/Marketing/Feature/Architecture HTML — that's the natural continuation, not something I could queue as more infrastructure PRDs.

This is a one-shot run, so I'm not tracking these to completion live (`/develop`'s Phase 2 watch loop) — they're queued and will run via Bilko's existing scheduler on its normal cadence. Next time this Epic's conversation resumes, check `session-manager-operations/scheduler/state/` or the two PRD files' run status before proceeding to Stage 1 summary computation.
